children: Qualcomm (QCOM) shares fell 2% Thursday after the semiconductor company renewed its global patent licensing arrangement with Apple (AAPL), extending a long-running commercial relationship, according to a Thursday press release.
The new agreement takes effect April 1, 2027. Qualcomm executive John Han said the company welcomed the extension, while the companies provided no additional financial details.
Licensing remains a notable revenue source for Qualcomm. The company generated $1.28 billion from technology licensing in its latest quarter, down 3% from a year earlier.

The renewal comes as Qualcomm's role in supplying modem chips to Apple has evolved. Apple started using its own C-series modem technology with the iPhone 16e in 2025, reducing its dependence on Qualcomm for those components.

The two companies have extended their patent licensing relationship several times, including in 2019. Thursday's agreement maintains that relationship as their broader hardware partnership continues to change.

title: What's Going On With Qualcomm Stock Thursday
